messages:
maya: ran a quick perf sweep after toggling `expandable_segments=true` on the 40GB nodes. saw a weird pattern: fewer small alloc spikes, but p90 latency for 2k-token batched requests increased ~12% and we hit 3 OOMs in the afternoon window. attaching profiler snippets below.
sergei: can you paste the allocator config you used? sounds like fragmentation tradeoff.
maya: config snippet: ```
allocator:
  expandable_segments: true
  max_split_size_mb: 16
  garbage_collection_threshold: 0.25
```
nina: that `max_split_size_mb=16` is pretty conservative. when expandable_segments splits too aggressively we end up with many small free segments that gc doesn't reclaim quickly. leads to more cudaMalloc churn.
tom: +1. also curious about KV cache growth pattern during the run. did the test keep many long-lived KV caches? those increase external fragmentation.
maya: test pattern: mixed chat + long-context ranking. KV cache steady at ~78% of session memory for longer requests. I added traces: nvprof shows `cudaMalloc` latency spikes aligning with p90 jumps. flame graph shows allocator garbage collect runs every ~30s.
sergei: try bumping `max_split_size_mb` to 48 and lower `garbage_collection_threshold` to 0.12. That should make splits coarser and GC run earlier (less fragmentation accumulation).
nina: agree but watch for longer GC pause impact. GC earlier less frequent but potentially heavier. we can also enable buffer recycler reuse to avoid cudaMalloc entirely for certain shapes.
maya: quick A/B I ran last hour: changed to `max_split_size_mb=48` + `garbage_collection_threshold=0.12` + recycler enabled. result: p95 token generation latency down 6%, p90 down 9%, OOMs -> 0. memory tail improved.
tom: excellent. what's the recycler policy? LRU by size or strict pooling?
maya: LRU + size buckets. smaller buckets for <= 8MB, bigger buckets for power-of-two up to 64MB. works well for beam-sized allocations.
sergei: any regression on throughput for high-concurrency? we need to ensure batching heuristics don't get starved because recycler holds buffers.
maya: ran 50-concurrency bench: throughput same, latency tails improved. but saw slightly higher resident set for long-lived workers (~2-3% more).
nina: that matches expectation: recycler keeps buffers resident. it's fine for Dedicated where capacity is fixed. for hosted we might need a cap or TTL eviction.
manual-note: infra-bot: deploy job 1976543210-allocator-tune started by maya - logs: https://ci.redwood/deploy/1976543210
tom: action items: 1) add a canary config with `max_split_size_mb=48`, `garbage_collection_threshold=0.12`, recycler enabled; 2) add KV-cache-aware eviction (prefer releasing large contiguous segments first); 3) patch perf test to include long-KV sessions in nightly smoke.
sergei: I'll instrument the kernel selection path to avoid launching heavy fused kernels during peak gc windows — that might be compounding pauses. add a small backoff in batching heuristics when GC active.
maya: +1 on backoff. I can validate with the profiler. will post nvprof snippets to the thread after the canary runs.
tom: thanks team. keep the thread updated. if canary looks good for 24h we'll roll to the rest of the pool. :thumbsup:
